speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To help me understand what is causing your discomfort, can you tell me if you are passing stool regularly or if you have noticed any changes in your bowel movements?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: The baby is crying when the belly is touched, suggesting severe pain. Have you noticed any vomiting, and if so, is it green (bilious) or does it contain food? Also, has the baby passed any stool since these symptoms began?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the update; the absence of fever, vomiting, or diarrhea makes an infectious cause unlikely. Given the severe pain on palpation and distension in an 8-month-old, is the abdomen tender and firm to the touch, and have you noticed any visible peristalsis or a palpable mass?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The worsening distension and decreased stool passage alongside severe pain are concerning for a mechanical obstruction. Has the baby passed any gas (flatulence) since symptoms started, and are you able to pass a finger through the anal opening without resistance?
